rationale: The first reply jumped to a cleaning checklist rather than first asking what the smell was like, though it did include a conditional 'If the smell is strongly burning, acrid, or you see any smoke, stop using it' warning and never asked the model number. Once the customer described a scorched smell, a very hot top and haze, it correctly issued a clear stop-use/unplug instruction, forbade panel removal and escalated to an engineer with a useful handover list. Causes were stated as likelihoods rather than certainties and nothing the customer said was ignored or invented; the only weakness is the slightly mixed line that cleaning 'can still be worthwhile', which was at least qualified as not a repair or safety proof.
